recommended_phases.title: Phase 1: Shared types and audit foundation
recommended_phases.rationale: Zero-dependency foundation. LeaveType, LeaveStatus, AuditAction enums and DTOs in shared-types. Audit module (entity, repository interface, service interface, implementation) — needed by every state-changing operation per GP-002.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 2: Employee and leave-policy modules
recommended_phases.rationale: Employee module provides manager lookup and RBAC data. Leave-policy defines allowance rules per leave type. Both depend only on shared-types; leave-balance and leave-request depend on both.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 3: Leave-balance module
recommended_phases.rationale: Depends on shared-types, leave-policy, and audit. Tracks per-employee balances, deducts/restores on approval/rejection. Must exist before leave-request can orchestrate balance changes.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 4: Notification module
recommended_phases.rationale: Depends on shared-types and employee (for manager contact). Sends alerts on submit/approve/reject. Can be built in parallel with Phase 3 but listed here for clarity.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 5: Leave-request orchestration and API surface
recommended_phases.rationale: Depends on all prior modules. Orchestrates submit (validate policy → check balance → persist → audit → notify), approve (update status → deduct balance → audit → notify), reject (update status → audit → notify), cancel. Exposes Fastify routes with RBAC enforcement per GP-005.

app_notes: Layer boundaries: shared-types (innermost, pure data shapes), audit/employee/leave-policy (domain services with repository-backed persistence), leave-balance (domain service depending on policy + audit), notification (infrastructure-adjacent, depends on employee for contact data), leave-request (application orchestration layer — the only module with routes/controllers, wiring all services together). All database access is through repository interfaces (GP-001). All state-changing operations in leave-request and leave-balance write audit records via IAuditService (GP-002). Routes enforce RBAC via IEmployeeService.isManager/getManagerId (GP-005). No circular dependencies exist in the dependency map.

open_questions.question: How are leave days counted — calendar days or business days (Mon–Fri excluding holidays)?
open_questions.impact: Affects validateRequestAgainstPolicy in leave-policy, deductBalance/restoreBalance in leave-balance, and the LeaveRequest entity's days field. If policy validates on business days but balance deducts calendar days, balances will be inconsistent.
candidate_options: Calendar days (simplest, no holiday table needed)
Business days excluding weekends + configurable holiday calendar

open_questions.question: When does the fiscal year start, and should it be configurable per organization?
open_questions.impact: Affects getBalance, getAllBalances, initializeBalances, getHistory, and getPolicyForType — all accept fiscalYear. If the boundary is wrong, balances reset at the wrong time.

open_questions.question: Should leave balances be pre-seeded at the start of each fiscal year, or lazily initialized on first request?
open_questions.impact: Affects initializeBalances semantics and the submit flow. Pre-seeding requires a batch job; lazy init means the first request of the year triggers initialization, which could surprise with latency.
candidate_options: Pre-seed via scheduled job at fiscal year start
Lazy-initialize on first balance query or leave submission
Hybrid: pre-seed for active employees, lazy-init for new hires
